payload.title: 30 Wedding Centrepieces That Make the Table
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: A couple in their thirties with a six-figure AUD budget and a destination wedding taking shape, who have saved dozens of centrepiece photos and now need to narrow them to one look that suits their actual tables, room and venue rules, so they can brief a florist or stylist they may only meet by video call.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about styling the reception: one click to the Wedded Concierge page from the closing line.
payload.angle: Page-one results are photo galleries with no reasoning. This guide starts with how to choose (table shape, height and sightlines, scale against the room, where the budget actually goes), then gives exactly 30 ideas grouped by style, each with a one-line 'works best on' note, and closes with the practical questions galleries skip and that matter more abroad: whether the venue allows open flame, scent and allergies near food, who sets up and packs down, reusing ceremony florals, and what to ask a local florist you have never met.
must_include: SECTION 'How to choose a centrepiece': (a) table shape, round versus long or banquet tables, and how each changes the brief (one focal piece versus a continuous run); (b) height and sightlines, keep arrangements low enough to talk over or lift them clear of eye level, never in between; (c) scale against the room, ceiling height, room size and guest count; (d) budget levers as advice only (fewer stems with more foliage, candles and greenery doing the work, repurposing ceremony pieces, mixing statement and simple tables), linking /style-advice/wedding-flowers-cost for cost detail. No figures, ranges or prices.

SECTION '30 wedding centrepiece ideas': EXACTLY 30 numbered ideas, numbered continuously 1 to 30 across seven groups: (1) low and lush florals; (2) tall and dramatic; (3) long-table garlands and runners; (4) candlelit; (5) fruit, foliage and edible; (6) non-floral (glass, sculpture, books, objects); (7) destination and local styling (for example shells, citrus, olive branches, written as styling ideas, never as claims about what a place grows, sells or is known for). Each idea: a short name, two to three sentences on the look, and a 'works best on' line (table shape or setting). Suggested split 5, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 4; the planner may rebalance but the total must be 30.

Flowers are named only as design choices (colour, shape, texture). Never say a flower is 'in season' or available at a time or place; link the flowers hub /fashionable-flowers-opt-for-in-season-or-order-imported for seasonality instead.

SECTION 'Practical details': (a) open flame, candles and hurricanes, ask the venue what it permits, as rules vary by venue; (b) allergies and strong scent near food, keep heavily scented blooms away from plates; (c) set-up and pack-down, who does it, when, and what happens to vessels and hire items afterwards; (d) reusing ceremony florals at the reception, and who moves them.

SECTION 'Centrepieces for a destination wedding': framed as questions to ask the venue and a local florist (what vessels and candle holders the venue holds; what must be hired in; flame and fixing rules; whether a local florist can work from a mood board and send a sample photo; what is sourced locally versus brought in; delivery and set-up timing). Questions only, no claims about any destination.

Internal links: /style-advice/wedding-table-decor linked prominently in the intro and again near the close as the guide to the whole table and room; /style-advice/22-amazing-table-settings-for-every-wedding-theme for place settings; /style-advice/wedding-flowers-cost for budget; flowers hub for seasons.

FAQ of 4 to 6 questions in the reader's words (for example how tall should centrepieces be, do long tables need one centrepiece or several, can we reuse ceremony flowers, can we use candles at our venue, non-floral options), answers as practical advice with no figures.

Close with ONE Wedded Advisor line drawn from brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30, for example that one Wedded Advisor plans venue, vendors and the details with them from start to finish and confirms inclusions in writing before they commit. One line, no hard sell.
avoid: Prices, cost ranges or any figures, including in the budget section
Vendor, florist, brand or venue names
Statistics, survey numbers, trend claims ('this year's trend', 'trending', 'on the rise')
Research talk ('we analysed', 'our research shows', 'search data')
Calling any flower 'in season' or claiming availability, unless a source is supplied
Claims about what a destination grows, is famous for or traditionally uses

Place settings detail (owned by the table settings post) and whole-room decor such as linen, chairs, lighting plans and signage (owned by /style-advice/wedding-table-decor); mention briefly and link out
Seasonal flower lists (owned by the flowers hub)
Competitor wording, claims or images; no Easy Weddings phrasing
Clichés such as fairytale, dream day, Pinterest-perfect, instaworthy
Em dashes; US spelling (centerpiece only where quoting the old URL slug, never in copy)
payload.cannibalisation_check: (1) /style-advice/wedding-table-decor targets 'wedding table decor' and lists centrepieces in its topic; it owns decor and the room. This post goes deep on the centrepiece only (30 ideas plus how to choose) and links to it prominently, so the decor page keeps the broad term and this page takes 'wedding centrepieces'. Recommend the decor page add a link back to this post (flag for the editor or link-map owner). (2) /centerpiece-alternatives-wedding-reception-2 (old, no primary keyword, conflicting noindex signals): overlaps the non-floral group; recommend a 301 into this post once live, team decision, and do not link to it. (3) /trending-centerpiece-cake (unchecked, cake as centrepiece): minor overlap, not linked; review at the SEO stage. (4) Table settings post owns place settings and the flowers hub owns seasons; no keyword overlap.
